rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.1, 3.1 and 3.3 <U+2014> the authors built and deployed their own IoT monitoring/decision-support system on eight drip-irrigated olive parcels in eastern Crete during 2021<U+2013>2022, collected soil-moisture, EC, temperature and weather data, and compared the platform's weekly irrigation-dose recommendations with manually calculated FAO-56 values for the 2022 irrigation season.
rows.notes: The study reports that the platform computes a weekly irrigation dose per tree (FAO-56 Penman-Monteith plus soil-moisture threshold check) and that these recommendations matched manual calculations for all parcels (Section 3.3). It does not measure actual water applied, water savings, water productivity or yield under platform-guided versus conventional scheduling; the statements about 'reduction of irrigation water losses' and 'increased water-use efficiency' (Section 3.3) are asserted benefits, not measured results. The study therefore supports only the precondition (the platform calculates crop water needs), not the claimed effect of efficient water use. The authors do state limitations (preliminary user testing, single crop, need to extend to other soils/climates), but these do not bear on a water-conservation result that was never measured.

notes: Full text appears complete, though the PDF extraction contains duplicated/overlapping text blocks on several pages. System-development/implementation paper; validation limited to agreement between platform outputs and manual calculations of the same equations.
